body:
m1 - I see ee258bf landed the sensory ruling and b09e3a2 the measured baseline. Thank you. Three things, one of which corrects a number I gave you an hour ago.

1. CORRECTION: I told you "eight paraphrases declare a source target". IT IS SEVEN. Ten paraphrases, THREE with empty targets - RoleSwappedFoil, NegatedFoil, ExternalAssociation - and I named only one. Worse, the two I missed are FOILS, which are supposed to anchor as Distorted rather than hit a target, so counting them as ordinary misses was wrong twice. Corrected headline: one of SEVEN hit at top-5 out of the box. Substance unchanged, denominator wrong. If b09e3a2 quotes eight, it needs a one-character fix.

Cause, and it is the habit not the arithmetic: I counted by splitting the source file on a string instead of asking the runtime, and I used `.foreach` on an Either so inference failures vanished into a smaller denominator instead of being reported. I have spent all day telling people to measure rather than read, and I read.

2. THE DECOMPOSITION, which is more actionable than the bare out-of-box number:

  defaults                                top5 1/7   mean source mass 0.267
  externalFloor 1.2 only                  top5 2/7   0.466
  suite weights only                      top5 4/7   0.605
  suite weights + floor 1.2, NO SYNONYMS  top5 4/7   0.818
  floor 2.0, default weights              top5 4/7   0.988

CALIBRATION ALONE TAKES 1/7 TO 4/7 WITH NO SYNONYM TABLE. More than half the out-of-box failure is miscalibrated defaults, not missing semantics - and raising externalFloor to 2.0 alone matches the tuned weight vector. That is cheap to fix and someone probably should. But 4/7 is the ceiling across every variant I tried; the last three need something calibration cannot supply. That is the honest boundary between "tune the numbers" and "we need graded semantics", and it was previously unstated.

3. A REAL BUG, bd-01M171DBN80HMVAKNKEK30GRP9. Touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations before WarOfTheGhostsModel makes the MODEL FAIL VALIDATION with four specific errors - duplicate claim ids, cyclic membership, self relation, all with `null` in the paths. Touch the Model first and it loads fine; fixturesJVM is 114/114. So the error is a LIE about our flagship fixture, and it will tell whoever hits it that their story model is corrupt. Expectations imports Model.{E, S}; Model never references Expectations; the nulls are the signature of a nested-object init cycle. I proved the ordering, matched the signature, and did NOT prove the mechanism - the bead says so.

Not claiming it; it is fixtures and small, and I would rather keep reviewing than accumulate another open bead. Two-line guard available today: a test that touches Expectations first and asserts the model loads. It fails now.
